steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Gustav Stresemann served as Chancellor for just 102 days (August-November 1923) but remained Foreign Secretary from August 1923 until his death on 3 October 1929. He was the dominant figure in German politics during the "Golden Years" and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1926 alongside French Foreign Minister Aristide Briand. | Key Fact: The Dawes Plan, negotiated by American banker Charles Dawes, restructured Germany's reparations payments. Annual payments were reduced from £50 million to a starting figure of £10 million, rising to £25 million over 5 years. Crucially, it also arranged American loans of 800 million gold marks to Germany. | Key Fact: The Locarno Pact was signed on 16 October 1925 in Locarno, Switzerland.
